name: loop-guard-classic-ab
question: Does the play-time loop guard cost us anything in real tournament games? We already know it helps on an empty board. At episode 2,000 it recovered 14.3 coins per game on coin-heaven and never collected fewer coins in any of 140 world-checkpoint pairs. On 20 classic worlds we saw no difference either way, but the interval was far too wide to rule out a real cost. This test is big enough to answer the question we actually care about before we ship anything.
hypothesis: We expect the guard to be neutral or slightly positive on classic. It only acts when our agent is stuck and no bomb or explosion is within five tiles, which covers little of a live game. Most of its effect should come after the opponents are dead, when the unguarded agent paces instead of collecting the remaining coins. The risk we are watching is self-kills: on coin-heaven the guard led the policy into new areas where it sometimes bombed itself.

checkpoints.also_played: the untrained reference, for context only; it does not enter the decision

suite.name: loop-guard-classic-fresh
suite.seed_audit: We checked all 100 seeds, and their +1,000,000 offsets, against every integer literal in the 907 tracked text files on 17 September. No collision. The only integers near the block were digit runs inside SHA-256 hashes. None of these worlds overlaps the held-out suite, and the evaluator refuses a registration that does.

secondary.suite: coin-heaven development worlds of the final-training registration, all 40
secondary.role: descriptive only. It tells us how much the guard gains on an empty board at episode 4,000. It cannot change the decision.

decision_rule.contrast: guarded minus unguarded, paired on the same checkpoint and world

interval.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap, resampling the six checkpoints and then the worlds

ship_if_all: the lower bound of the score interval is above -0.30
the score point estimate is at least 0
the upper bound of the self-kill interval is at most +0.10
decision_rule.otherwise: The guard does not ship in this form, and Bomb-omb stays identical to the agent we trained.
decision_rule.why_these_numbers: 0.30 points is about a tenth of what our trained agents score against three rule_based agents, and it is the most we are willing to give up for better solo play. A self-kill bound of +0.10 per game keeps the cost we saw on coin-heaven from quietly growing on classic.

known_limits: Opponents are not seeded. The same world still plays out differently each time, so part of every difference is noise.
Only six checkpoints, so the checkpoint level dominates the interval. An inconclusive result is a real possibility, and under this rule it means we do not ship the guard.
We judge the guard on episode-4,000 checkpoints. If we later ship a much later milestone, this result carries over as evidence but is not a direct test of that checkpoint.
expected_cost: about 1,400 classic games and 560 coin-heaven games, roughly an hour on a laptop with two jobs
authorization: Julius (1BlauNitrox) asked for this test on 17 September 2026 and runs it on the second laptop.
